effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative probabilistic scenario estimates and entropy-reduction (ER) sensitivity metrics from discretized Bayesian networks on N = 101 countries; no frequentist confidence intervals or p-values are reported because the models compute Bayesian conditional probabilities.
effect_estimate.value: Across N = 101 developing countries (2004 cross-section), baseline probabilities of high water supply access (WS > 82%) and high sanitation access (S > 58%) are 48.6% and 45.8%, respectively, with sanitation trailing water supply linearly across countries (S = 1.0285 WS - 21.82, adjusted R^2 = 0.5265). Setting Human Development and Poverty (HDP, integrating advanced governance WGI-GE and % slums) to 100% HIGH raises the probability of high WS access to 84.5% (+35.9 percentage points; entropy reduction ER = 0.36475, rank 1) and high S access to 80.3% (+34.5 percentage points; ER = 0.3201, rank 1). Setting Country Environmental Concern (CEC, integrating voice/accountability WGI-VA and international environmental agreement participation) to 100% HIGH raises high WS probability to 70.3% (+24.1 percentage points in Table 10; ER = 0.06549, rank 2) and high S probability to 53.9% (+8.1 percentage points; ER = 0.01982, rank 3). Within the HDP submodel (baseline high HDP = 20.2%), setting % slums to 100% LOW raises high HDP probability to 51.9% (+31.9 percentage points in Table 10; ER = 0.51033, rank 3) and setting advanced governance (WGI-GE: government effectiveness, rule of law, regulatory quality, corruption control) to 100% HIGH raises high HDP probability to 44.7% (44.5% in text; +24.8 percentage points in Table 10; ER = 0.26849). Within the CEC submodel (baseline high CEC = 30.8%), setting civil society voice and accountability (WGI-VA) to 100% HIGH raises high CEC probability to 54.4% (+23.8 percentage points in Table 10; ER = 0.37631).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional country-level observational Bayesian network study (capped at <= 2). Assigned 1 because the study documents macro-level statistical/probabilistic associations among national governance indicators (WGI-GE, WGI-VA, WGI-PSAV), slum prevalence (% slums), aid flows (ODA-CI), and national WSS access, while explicitly noting that underlying causal mechanisms are hypothesized from simulations and external literature rather than directly observed at administrative or household level.

study_design.comment: Observational cross-country cross-sectional analysis modeling 25 discretized national indicators (k-means into low/mid/high categories) and PCA-derived thematic composite indicators using general directed acyclic graph (DAG) Bayesian networks and naive Bayes classifiers, validated via classification error rates and evaluated through entropy-reduction sensitivity analysis and conditional probability scenario simulations.
study_design.value: Cross-national observational cross-sectional study using Bayesian network probabilistic graphical modelling (directed acyclic graphs and naive Bayes classifiers as a non-parametric regression alternative) with sensitivity analysis and probabilistic scenario simulations
